moves.name: Stand LP
extraInfo: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

moves.name: Stand MP
extraInfo: Primary combo and frame trap starter
Great meaty tool with 4 active frames (up to +9 on Hit / +4 on Block)
Leaves C. Viper in throw range on block
but all characters can walk back to make the throw whiff
Great approach tool out of Drive Rush for continued strike/throw pressure

moves.name: Stand HP
extraInfo: Long range poke that can be Super Jump canceled into Feint or Seismic Hammer for high damage combos
C. Viper's only Feint cancel that is plus on block

moves.name: Stand LK
extraInfo: Primary 5F punish tool and link option after chained light normals (can link after Crouch LP in 4-hit light confirms)
Higher hitstun than other light normals (combos naturally into MP Thunder Dash)
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

moves.name: Stand MK
extraInfo: Strong poke and whiff punish tool that can be Super Jump canceled for more damage
Combos into 2HP when SJC'd (Super Jump canceled) after a whiff punishing something (Punish Counter)
Counter-hit allows a link to SA2 or a SJC into LP Seismic Hammer
+2F extra recovery frames (20F) on whiff

moves.name: Stand HK
extraInfo: Puts airborne opponents into an OTG juggle state on hit
Stagger state on Punish Counter (+19)
Shorter range against crouching opponents
Can be juggled into after Seismo + SJC Air Burn Kick
then Super Jump canceled for further damage (SJC into grounded OD Burn Kick is a 2F timing window that's part of many optimal combo routes)
Punish Counter advantage is big enough to allow for a Super Jump cancel into a full jump-in combo

moves.name: Crouch LP
extraInfo: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo
Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-6 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)
1F extra hitstun (and frame advantage) than stand LP but has less range
Can be used as the third hit of a chain that links into stand LK
but this will whiff if the opponent stand blocks (also whiffs under many reversal standing jabs at this range)

moves.name: Crouch MP
extraInfo: Great hitstun for a 6F medium normal (combos into OD Seismic Hammer)
Topmost hurtboxes on frames 1-8 are vulnerable only to airborne attacks (this is to discourage its use as an anti-air)

moves.name: Crouch HP
extraInfo: Forces stand on hit
Viper's main special cancelable poke and combo tool (combos naturally into meterless Seismic Hammer)
Viper's core tool for FFF (Fierce Feint Fierce) combo routes

moves.name: Crouch LK
extraInfo: Chains into stand LP / crouch LP / crouch LK
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo
Crazy good frame advantages for a crouch LK
Pseudo-special-cancelable due to Super Jump (this SJC has relaxed execution requirements and can be performed with a simple Up input from a crouching state)

moves.name: Crouch MK
extraInfo: Long range low poke (furthest range crouch MK in the game that's still pseudo-special-cancelable) that can be Super Jump canceled for a combo extension (this SJC has relaxed execution requirements and can be performed with a simple Up input from a crouching state)
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo
Has good advantage on block when used from Drive Rush (but the high pushback keeps C. Viper out of throw range)

moves.name: Crouch HK
extraInfo: +4F extra recovery frames (29F) on block
Cannot be Super Jump canceled for safety
Punish Counter sets up a KD +45 safe jump using High Jump normals
Has some Juggle potential naturally without Drive Rush (like after OD Seismo for a meterless combo extension)

moves.name: Jump LP
extraInfo: Good close range air-to-air for opponents slightly above C. Viper

moves.name: Jump MP
extraInfo: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state
Cancelable into Air Burn Kick during a forward or neutral jump
Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-22

moves.name: Jump HP
extraInfo: Spikes down airborne opponents on hit
Strong hitbox priority for vertical approaches
Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 11-23

moves.name: Jump LK
extraInfo: Can be used as a fuzzy instant Overhead
Combos naturally from any close-range Super Jump canceled normal against Standing tall characters (JP
Marisa
Sagat
Zangief)
Very strong hitbox priority

moves.name: Jump MK
extraInfo: Cross-up
Great all-purpose jump-in (C. Viper's longest range forward jump normal) with exceptional hitbox priority
Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 7-20

moves.name: Jump HK
extraInfo: Cross-up
Cancelable into Air Burn Kick until the 37th airborne frame of jump or super jump (does not work in safe jump setups or on crouching opponents)
Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 8-19

moves.name: Neutral Jump HK
extraInfo: Furthest horizontal range and strongest horizontal hitbox priority of all of C. Viper's jump normals (although the effective horizontal range is very limited due to only being accessible from a Neutral jump)
Projectile invincible on lower body (legs) on frames 10-19

moves.name: Viper Elbow
extraInfo: Overhead
Crushes lows on frames 16-27 (not airborne or throw invincible)

moves.name: Double Kick
extraInfo: 2 hits
Carries over Counter-Hit / Punish Counter bonus frame advantage to both hits
Useful approach tool from Drive Rush that grants a strike/throw mixup on block or a Crouch MP link on hit
Minimal pushback gives this a lot of uses cases on hit or block
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo

moves.name: High Impulse
extraInfo: Grants a corner throw loop with forward dash (+7) or walking with manual timing
Can pressure with meaty Burning Kick + Double Burn (+2 oB): MK version makes the follow-up a true blockstring
while HK version leaves a small blockstring gap that can bait Drive Impact
Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage
Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up)
depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent
and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker
Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

moves.name: Thunder Cradle
extraInfo: No real oki after a corner side switch (but can pressure with Drive Rush normals)
Can pressure with meaty LK Burning Kick into Double Burn (+2 oB) (punishable with wakeup Drive Impact
but opponent cannot DI punish the Double Burn)
Punish Counter gives +70% (2040) damage
Hard Knockdown (denies back-roll option on wake-up)
depletes 1 bar of Drive gauge from the opponent
and builds twice as much Super gauge for the attacker
Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender (randomly assigned if throws are input simultaneously)

moves.name: Drive Impact: Viper Cannon
extraInfo: 2 hits of armor on frames 1-27
Damages opponents Drive Gauge on Block (1/2 bar) | Hit (1 bar) | Counter-Hit (1.25 bar) | Punish Counter (1.5 bar)
Knocks down on hit
Pushes the opponent far back on hit or block and causes a Wall Splat if they hit the wall (Parry prevents the backwards stumble and Wall Splat
greatly reducing the pushback)
Regular KDA without Wall Splat +35 KD | Wall Splat on Hit +65 KD | Wall Splat on Block +72 HKD
KDA can vary greatly depending on how high the opponent wall splats (higher KDA the higher they wall splat)
Advantage after Wall Splat can vary depending on distance from the corner (farther from corner gives higher advantage)
Crumples the opponent on Punish Counter or after absorbing at least 1 attack during start-up (+21 frames before the crumple state goes airborne
followed by airborne state on frames 22-46 before they are grounded)
Puts airborne opponents into a long spinning free juggle state when hit as a Punish Counter or after absorbing an attack

If the armor absorbs an attack it slows the overall start-up by 1F (27F total instead of 26F) and incurs 6F hitstop for each projectile hit absorbed (making it less likely to punish the opponent after absorbing projectiles)
Absorbing an attack causes the player to take 1/2 the damage in recoverable health (but will KO if this would bring the player's health below zero)
Stun/Dizzy occurs when a Wall Splat connects on an opponent in Burnout
Stun gives a free combo follow-up for the next 195F after hitting the wall
followed by a HKD if the player falls to the ground untouched (the last 7F before hitting the ground has a crouch-sized hurtbox but is considered standing
allowing for unique combo setups)
Incurs 20% damage scaling penalty if used as the first hit of a combo (applies to wall splat on HIT
crumple
Burnout dizzy on hit/block
or any character-specific means of comboing after a regular Drive Impact)
Incurs a 20% multiplier damage scaling penalty after a Wall Splat on BLOCK - Because the blocked Drive Impact is not considered a "hit" for the combo
the next attack can incur its own separate damage scaling as a combo starter

Wall Splat puts opponent into a special juggle state where the next move freely connects and continues the juggle even if it normally wouldn't (similar to a Forced Knockdown or Drive Rush juggle properties)
Does not cause Wall Splat if the Drive Impact connects as a combo or a true blockstring with no gaps (LOCK icon appears on-screen)

It is possible to "combo" into Stun if the opponent has under 1.5 Drive bars - a blocked DI Wall Splat from slightly outside the corner into a second DI on hit will cause Burnout and Stun (because the blocked DI is not technically considered a combo starter)
Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge
Cinematic slowdown occurs if both players activate Drive Impact within range of each other (granting a Punish Counter to the player who activates it later)
Attempting to counter with DI vs. DI with under 400 HP will result in a KO
as the second player will not have enough health to absorb it
Clashes with other Drive Impacts and refunds the Drive gauge cost if they collide on the same active frame (start at exactly the same time
or 1F apart if the first Drive Impact absorbs a strike) - The meter refund does not prevent Burnout from occurring
The scrub killer

moves.name: Drive Reversal: Counter Spark
extraInfo: Has two versions: one performed during blockstun or parry stun (20F start-up) and one performed as a wake-up reversal (18F start-up)
Fully invincible on frames 1-22 (blockstun) / frames 1-20 (reversal)
Armor Break (blows through all armor like Drive Impact
but not counters like JP's Amnesia)
Trying to Drive Reversal after the blockstun ends results in a Drive Impact
Drive Reversal immediately removes the current blockstun you're in and starts the attack
Causes a 4F screen freeze after the 6th start-up frame
which allows the opponent to perform a simple OS (inputting their buttons during the buffer window) to prevent their next attack from coming out
Safe on block (-2) when used against an opponent in Burnout
Costs 2 bars of Drive Gauge
If the opponent tries to throw against a wake-up Drive Reversal
it causes a 12F screen freeze and refunds 1 bar of Drive gauge (but does not prevent Burnout)
Guaranteed to interrupt any Drive Rush canceled normal if performed immediately out of blockstun (unless the opponent reacts with an invincible move or counter)

moves.name: Drive Parry
extraInfo: Parries all strikes and projectiles (high and low) from frame 1
12F parry window (can hold the parry to extend the parry window)
Perfect Parry occurs on the first 2 active frames (cannot achieve Perfect Parry if you buffer into parry by holding it during Reversal windows; Perfect Parries have to be timed properly)
Can still hold charge directions during Parry (allowing characters with charge specials to stand block before performing their reversal)
Can block during the recovery frames of a regular parry (can still get hit during the recovery frames if you don't block correctly)
Getting thrown or hit at any point during the recovery frames of a whiffed parry attempt results in a Punish Counter
Successfully parrying a move puts you into the same amount of blockstun as that move would regularly do on block (but a Perfect Parry has only 1F of recovery)
Throw invincible during the recovery of a successful parry (just like during blockstun)
Perfect Parrying a strike has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack (basically a guaranteed punish opportunity except for safe jump setups)
Perfect Parrying a strike requires holding the correct block direction (Down+Back for low strikes
Back for high/mid strikes)
Attempting a Perfect Parry with the wrong block direction results in an "imperfect parry" that builds an extra 3000 Drive Gauge and plays a distinct audio/visual cue
After a successful Perfect Parry
you suffer a 50% penalty to your Damage
Drive Gauge Generation
and Drive Gauge Damage on any of your following attacks when punishing the opponent (in addition
both you and the opponent suffer a 20% penalty to your Super Meter gain during this period)
Fully invincible for 6F after a successful Perfect Parry against a strike
which carries over to any attack you perform (ensuring a 5F or faster punish will always interrupt multi-hit attacks)
Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 10 frames of recovery and applies the same 50% scaling penalties (and 20% Super Meter penalty) on your following attacks when punishing the opponent
Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will result in a regular parry for the strike attack (effectively ignoring the projectile's hitstop / blockstun)
Perfect Parrying a Strike and Projectile on the same frame will give a screen freeze like you Perfect Parried a Strike
but still give you 10F recovery as if you had Perfect Parried a Projectile
Can cancel into Drive Rush during active frames 3 and onward (fastest Drive Rush method is to buffer a forward input before doing parry + forward again)
Can cancel into Drive Reversal from a successful parry (just like you normally can during blockstun)
Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge and continues to deplete 50 Drive Gauge per frame (0.3 Drive bars per second) as you hold the Parry
You lose the parry if you go into Burnout from the initial Drive Gauge cost (Perfect Parry requires frame-perfect timing when starting from under 1/2 of a Drive bar)
Rewards 1 bar of Drive Gauge (1/2 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a strike
Rewards 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge (0 bar total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successfully parrying a projectile (with a few exceptions)
Rewards 2 bars of Drive Gauge (1.5 bars total after factoring in the initial parry cost) for successful parrying a Super Art or Drive Impact
Successfully parrying a strike attack splits the regular block pushback between both players (while Perfect Parrying a strike removes all of its pushback)
Successfully parrying a projectile or Drive Impact reduces the pushback of it by half (while Perfect Parrying a projectile or Drive Impact removes all of its pushback)
Your hurtbox and throw box expand slightly towards the opponent for the entire duration of the Parry (Throw box extension starts instantly on frame 1
while the Hurtbox extension starts on frame 3
after the initial 2F Perfect Parry window)
Parrying while crouching maintains a regular crouch hurtbox for the first 2 frames of the parry (during the initial Perfect Parry window)

moves.name: Drive Rush
extraInfo: Dashes forward and enhances the next normal or command normal used out of the Drive Rush with +4 extra hitstun / blockstun
as well as improved juggle properties (Juggle Limit increased by +3 / Juggle Start/Increase reduced to 0)
The +4 bonus frame advantage gained from a Drive Rush enhanced move also stacks with any bonus frame advantage that move may have gained from Counter-Hit
Punish Counter
or Burnout
Grounded special-cancelable normals can also be canceled into Drive Rush on hit or block
as well as from light normals on whiff
Drive Rush maintains buffers (freezes the buffer window) during its start-up and freeze frames - This allows players to do things normally not possible within the normal buffer windows
such as Drive Rushing into a charge special

The initial 10F screen freeze eats the opponent's directional inputs (except Jumps) but does not prevent attacks from being buffered immediately afterward (this can cause inputs to be combined in unintended ways
such as crouch MK + Fireball performing a raw Fireball
or a vertical jump + walk forward turning into a forward jump)
Framedata shown in parentheses refers to the Drive Rush version used from a Parry

Drive Rush recovery is only 24F total (23F if done from a Parry) - but the enhanced dash itself is 46F total (45F if done from Parry) and you can cancel it as early as frame 9 (frame 11 if done from a Parry)

Inputting a direction (walk/crouch/block/jump) after the Drive Rush recovery plays out 2 additional recovery frames before the transition occurs (this allows the user to perform an enhanced crouching or command normal late in the dash by inputting the direction + button simultaneously)

You stop building any form of Drive Gauge on your attacks after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (but you still continue to build Drive gauge as normal if you did Drive Rush at the START of a combo)
Applies an extra damage scaling penalty after using a Drive Rush in the MIDDLE of a combo (no damage scaling if you use Drive Rush at the START of a combo)
Costs 3 bars of Drive Gauge if canceled into from a normal attack
Costs 1/2 bar of Drive Gauge if canceled into from Parry (for a total of 1 bar of Drive Gauge when you factor in the initial 1/2 bar cost of the Parry)
Normals used out of Drive Rush carry additional forward momentum (but throws and specials immediately halt all momentum
which can be a useful strategy to punish opponents for trying to interrupt your Drive Rush)
Parry Drive Rush can only be initiated after frame 3 of the Parry (but can be performed immediately after recovering from a successful parry)

Parry Drive Rush cannot be initiated with less than 1/2 of a Drive bar (as the initial Parry cost will put the user into Burnout) - But whiff canceling a Light normal into Drive Rush can achieve a similar effect
Cannot cancel Drive Rush into a Parry (inputting MP+MK results in a MK normal coming out instead)
Drive Rush puts the user into a counter-hit state for the entire duration (this makes it impossible to tech a throw that connects during the dash)

moves.name: LP Thunder Dash
extraInfo: Upper body is projectile invincible on frames 14-20
Crouch size hurtboxes on frames 14-43 (but still counts as in Standing state)
Can be used to slip past certain Projectiles (C. Viper can get clipped in the back by the slower Projectiles) and potentially convert into a full combo on Punish Counter
Solid range for a neutral tool but must be spaced to remain safe on block
Does not count as a Low attack (despite looking like it might)
+2 on hit and keeps the opponent in range for a strike / throw pressure afterwards
Startup is cancelable into feint after 12F
Cancelable into Tracer Combination (f+PP) on hit or block

moves.name: MP Thunder Dash
extraInfo: Combos naturally from Stand LK
Less range than LP version but is safer as a buffer tool
Startup is cancelable into feint after 8F
Cancelable into Tracer Combination (f+PP) on hit or block

moves.name: HP Thunder Dash
extraInfo: Invincible to airborne attacks on frames 1-9
Airborne on frames 9-31 (Forced Knockdown state)
Combos naturally from light normals
Startup is cancelable into feint after 6F (gives the best advantage for combos and block pressure)

The Feint version's 6F anti-air invincibility can be used to effectively spot dodge certain airborne attacks from the opponent and get better Punish opportunities as a result (this usually requires precise timing and/or spacing)
Cancelable into Tracer Combination (f+PP) on hit only (can whiff against high airborne opponents)
Cannot hit cross-up (behind C. Viper)
Puts the opponent into a limited juggle state on hit

moves.name: OD Thunder Dash
extraInfo: 2 hits
1st hit has range in between LP/MP versions
Combos naturally from medium/heavy normals allowing a safe
easy hitconfirm into SA2 or SA3
Cannot perform a feint cancel or Tracer Combination follow-up
Great chip and pressure tool against Burnout (leaves C. Viper inside throw range at +2 on Block)
Has an extremely disjointed forward hitbox that can beat most pokes when used at midrange
Sets up a KD +42 safe jump on grounded hit (can only reach with max range Jump MK if midscreen)

moves.name: LP Tracer Combination
extraInfo: Follow-up maintains the Projectile invincibility and Crouch size hurtboxes on frames 1-17 (frames 14-37 overall)
Both hits are a true blockstring
Only follow-up that can combo into SA3 on grounded opponents
Gives solid oki with Drive Rush or Dash + manually timed walk
No Drive gauge cost during SA1 install and gains 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block

moves.name: MP Tracer Combination
moves.hcWinNotes: *Both hits, no combo on grounded opponent
extraInfo: Small gap between hits on block if not spaced out or connecting on last 2 active frames (risky -3 oB frame trap option to stop opponents from taking their turn)
Cannot combo into SA3 on grounded opponents
Limited juggle OTG bounce on airborne opponents (allows combo into SA3 when juggled into)
Gives the worst oki of all follow-ups on a grounded hit (-3 after dash)
No Drive gauge cost during SA1 install and gains 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block

moves.name: HP Tracer Combination
extraInfo: Can only be performed on hit
Follow-up can whiff on high airborne opponents
Gives the best oki of all Thunder Dash follow-ups on hit
No Drive gauge cost during SA1 install and gains 0.3 Drive bars on hit

moves.name: LK Burning Kick
extraInfo: Cannot hit cross-up
Airborne on frames 5-34 (Forced Knockdown state)
Lower body is projectile invincible on frames 14-27
Shortest range version primarily useful for beating throw techs and crouching buttons (connects from about C. Viper's max poke range)
Very difficult to space for better advantage due to minimal forward movement during active frames
Higher float on Punish Counter (+5 KD advantage and combos into KK follow-up)

Higher float on Punish Counter (+5 KD advantage and combos into KK follow-up)

moves.name: OD Burning Kick
extraInfo: 2 hits (cannot be interrupted on block)

moves.name: Knuckled Pursuit

Higher KD Advantage if Burning Kick hits airborne opponent or lands as a Punish Counter (+1 extra KD Advantage on Punish Counter)
Grants +9 KD Advantage when connecting on a grounded opponent after Burning Kick is absorbed by armor

If Burning Kick is blocked on a later active frame

Knockdown Advantage varies greatly depending on opponents height from the ground (higher advantage the higher up in the air the opponent is) as well as how how late into the active frames the move connects
Grants +40 KD Advantage if this follow-up kick connects on a grounded opponent (like if the opponent doesn't block this follow-up kick)

Distance varies based on button strength: LP close | MP ~50% screen | HP ~80% screen (all versions stop at the corner)

extraInfo: Has 1 hit of armor on frames 6-13 or until release
Absorbing a strike results in an automatic 10F counter-attack that comes out on frame 14 at the earliest (may be blocked if a light normal is absorbed early in the armor frames)
Cancelable into forward dash on frames 12-14 or until button is released (cannot dash after absorbing a strike)
C. Viper is in a Punish Counter state for the entire duration (including a forward dash cancel)
Slightly increased oki on Punish Counter
Button can be held to extend the armor and dash cancel frames (up to frame 59) and changing various properties of the move (see the lvl 2 / lvl 3 versions of this move for more details)
Only the first hit gains extra damage on Punish Counter
Only the second hit causes a Knockdown (can sometimes trade on the first hit
which can result in a follow-up combo for C. Viper)

Useful tool against Drive Impact while in Burnout (though the armor starts too late to work in most DI cancel blockstrings)
17 on Punish Counter if only the first hit reaches the opponent (e.g. absorbing a ranged Dhalsim poke)
This move cannot be performed if input while still holding down any Punch button on Classic Controls (this is to help prevent accidentally getting this move instead of a SJC feint)

moves.name: Feint
extraInfo: This feint can be canceled into during the start-up of Thunder Dash (214P) or Seismic Hammer (623P)
The feint itself has a duration of 12F (Thunder Dash) or 16F (Seismic Hammer)
but the Feint cancel window on each aforementioned Special is slightly different
resulting in different total duration for the Feint
Total feint duration: LP Thunder Dash 24F (12+12) / MP Thunder Dash 20F (8+12) / HP Thunder Dash 18F (6+12) / Seismic Hammer 27F (11+16)
C. Viper is in a counter-hit state for the entire feint duration

The K button can be held to automatically feint at the earliest possible timing (can result in accidental Focus Force activation when performed from a Super Jump cancel even without negative edge enabled)

moves.name: High Jump
extraInfo: Cancelable into from any grounded normals (except Sweep
Overhead
and f+HK) and Seismic Hammer (623P) on Hit / Block (this cancel is notated by 'sj' (Super Jump) in the cancel data section of other moves)
Jumps slightly higher and ~50% farther than normal jump
The start-up of the jump itself is cancelable into any Special or Super during pre-jump frames 2-6 (2F pre-jump > follow-ups)
Airborne on frames 7-46 (Forced Knockdown state)
Counter-hit state for entire duration including prejump and landing recovery
Has 3 landing recovery frames like a standard jump
Can only be performed as a Forward or Neutral jump (canceling into Super Jump with an Up+Back input results in a vertical Super Jump)
Costs 1 bar of Drive Gauge to perform (but is free of cost during the Limit Decoupler (SA1) install)
This High Jump functions like OD Specials
momentarily freezing the Drive Gauge's passive build-up
but still allowing C. Viper to build back some of the Drive Gauge she just spent on the follow-up hits
Because the pre-jump frames 2-6 are Special cancelable
it means C. Viper can effectively make all her normals (except Sweep
Overhead
and f+HK) Special cancelable (even when they're not Special cancelable normals)
The upwards direction has to be input no later than 8F after any downwards direction in order to execute this Super Jump

Execution requirements are relaxed when canceled from a normal that is not otherwise special-cancelable (most notably crouch MK / crouch LK which can perform a SJC by tapping Up from a crouching state)
Can perform safe jump setups with High Jump (requires KD Advantage of +45)
BUG?: Burn Kicks (grounded or airborne) cannot be easily buffered into like all the other Specials performed from a Super Jump Cancel
but rather the Kick input has to be delayed until after the Super Jump script starts

and the Grounded Burn Kick versions can only be executed if the Kick is input on frames 2-3 of the pre-jump frames (this is a 2F window that's required for many of C. Viper's optimal damage conversions - For some reason
there is no button buffer accepted on frame 1 of the Super Jump script)

moves.name: Limit Decoupler
extraInfo: Strike and Throw invincible on frames 1-11 and further invincible to airborne strikes on frames 12-20
Armor Break
Depletes 0.5 Drive Bar on hit for the opponent
Temporarily grants C. Viper the ability to use any of her 1-bar moves (High Jump
Tracer Combination
Knuckled Pursuit
or Double Burn) at no cost to the Drive Gauge (doing this while in Burnout allows C. Viper only a single free move usage
which then ends the install timer)
These 1-bar attack follow-ups also build 0.3 Drive bars on hit or block while the install is active
Install has a timed duration of 700 frames (~11.7 seconds) which freezes during any hitstop or cinematics
The install becomes active on frame 21 (after active frames) on hit
block
or whiff
C. Viper does not build any Super meter while this install is active (it might even be smart to save up to two levels of Super before activating this install
in order to be able to do another SA1 before the install timer ends to extend the overall install duration)
If the first hit trades with a projectile at close range
it's possible for C. Viper to pick up a limited juggle like HP Thunder Dash
or Level 1/2 Super (depends on spacing / pushback / projectile hitstun)
